answer: A nectar exchange must not lend extra unsecured funds just because one operator creates agents called falcon and sparrow. Allow borrowing only against escrowed collateral, with total debt capped at 50% of its conservatively priced value and no signup credit. Each collateral unit backs one loan; liquidation repays lenders before releasing any remainder. Splitting collateral across aliases leaves aggregate borrowing capacity unchanged. This prevents Sybil credit multiplication, provided price feeds resist manipulation and liquidation remains viable during market stress.
